gaps.sentence: 'No, I won't open the door,' he said. He ___ to open the door.
gaps.explanation: Refusals are reported with refuse + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Sit down, please,' the nurse said to me. The nurse asked me ___ down.
gaps.explanation: Requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive: asked me to sit down.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'I can't find my passport anywhere,' she moaned. She moaned that she ___ find her passport anywhere.
gaps.explanation: Negative can backshifts to couldn't in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'You can rely on me,' she assured me. She assured me that I ___ rely on her.
gaps.explanation: Can backshifts to could after the past reporting verb 'assured'.

gaps.sentence: 'You broke my phone!' she said to her brother. She ___ her brother of breaking her phone.
'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
gaps.explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).
